findings.summary: Required Linux job is named 'linux (Release, x86_64, Clang)', not the planned 'linux (Release, x86_64)' (carried over, unchanged)
findings.scenario: The user sets branch protection from the plan's name and it never matches a reported check, so the Linux leg is silently not required. The name is stated in the PR body, so the user must use that exact string.

findings.summary: The informational GCC job (continue-on-error) reports a failed check run on every PR, although the workflow run concludes success (carried over; seen again on run 38103538920 for this head)
findings.scenario: Every PR shows a red X for 'linux (... GCC 14, informational - known sol2 bug)', which can mask a real new failure in that leg and conflicts with a 'CI-green before merge' rule unless that check is explicitly excluded.

findings.summary: On POSIX, LastErrorWasTimeout counts ETIMEDOUT as a receive timeout (carried over, unchanged)
findings.scenario: On Linux, recv failing with ETIMEDOUT means the connection died, so IsClosedByServer returns false for a dead connection. Practically unreachable on loopback; EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK alone is the SO_RCVTIMEO case.
